title: Prospective randomized blinded exploratory study comparing two remplissage techniques in arthroscopic Bankart repair for patients with anteroinferior shoulder instability: conventionally knotted 2 × 1.6 mm FiberTak anchors versus interconnected knotless 2 × 2.7 mm FiberTak anchors
summary:
Anteroinferior shoulder instability can lead to recurrent dislocation or subluxation of the shoulder. It is frequently associated with a Hill-Sachs lesion, a bony defect of the humeral head. Surgical stabilization can be performed using arthroscopic Bankart repair combined with an additional remplissage procedure. During remplissage, the posterior joint capsule and the infraspinatus tendon are fixed into the Hill-Sachs lesion.
This study compares two established remplissage techniques: a conventionally knotted technique using two 1.6-mm FiberTak anchors and an interconnected knotless technique using two 2.7-mm FiberTak anchors. A total of 40 patients will be randomly assigned to one of the two treatment groups. Clinical outcomes will be assessed before surgery and at 6, 12, and 24 months after surgery. In addition, MRI will be performed 6 months after surgery to assess the structural integrity of the remplissage. The aim of the study is to investigate whether the two techniques differ in terms of clinical outcomes and structural integrity of the reconstruction.
conditions: Habitual/recurrent dislocation or subluxation of the shoulder

interventions.name: Bankart-Repair + Remplissage with 2 × 1,6 mm conventionally knotted FiberTak anchors
Bankart-Repair + Remplissage with 2 × 2.7 mm FiberTak conventionally knotted anchors

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Anteroinferior shoulder instability with a clinical and imaging-based indication for arthroscopic stabilization using Bankart repair and remplissage. 
Age 18 to 60 years. 
Planned surgery at the Department of Orthopaedics and Trauma Surgery, Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin, Campus Charité Mitte or Campus Virchow-Klinikum, during the study period. 
Ability to participate in follow-up examinations and complete the questionnaires. 
Written informed consent after receiving study information.
Exclusion criteria:
Revision surgery following previous shoulder stabilization surgery. 
Relevant bony glenoid defects requiring a different surgical strategy. 
Concomitant pathologies substantially affecting the outcome, e.g. high-grade rotator cuff tear or advanced osteoarthritis. 
Neurological or systemic diseases substantially affecting shoulder function. 
Contraindications to MRI of the shoulder, e.g. certain metallic implants or severe claustrophobia. 
Pregnancy.
